pretexts: grandchild or family member arrested and needs bail money
loved one has trouble returning from foreign country
family member's phone is broken and needs money for repair or bills
caller impersonates law enforcement official or lawyer on behalf of family member
family member needs money for lawyer fees, hospital fees, or ambulance fees
emerging_tactics: broken phone pretext via text or social media
social media reconnaissance to gather family details

kill_chain_signals.contact: Phone call typically on home phone/landline, or email/text message claiming to be loved one
kill_chain_signals.pretext: Claim family member arrested, in accident, or phone broken; use urgency and gag order to prevent verification
kill_chain_signals.payment: Request cash, cryptocurrency, or gift cards immediately
kill_chain_signals.movement: Arrange to pick up funds in person or ask victim to send cash in mail
kill_chain_signals.cashout: Fraudsters collect cash or cryptocurrency directly from victim

red_flags: Caller uses urgency and threats to convince you to take out money immediately
Claim there is a gag order preventing you from speaking about the situation
Caller provides alternate phone number instead of using known contact
Request for bail payment in cash or cryptocurrency (not allowed in Canadian Criminal Justice System)
Caller ID may be spoofed to appear as trusted number
key_quote: Emergency frauds prey on your fear of a loved one being hurt or in trouble.
title: Emergency
